found_and_fixed.title: JSON-LD structured data still claimed the business speaks Hebrew
found_and_fixed.detail: components/JsonLd.tsx's TaxiService schema had `availableLanguage: ["he", "en", "ru"]`. The prior session (mobile-fixes.json, MOB-06) deliberately removed the 'we speak Hebrew' claim from 6 visible places on the site because staff don't actually speak Hebrew, but missed this one -- it's inside <script type="application/ld+json"> so it doesn't show up in a normal read-through of visible page text. This is exactly the kind of claim MOB-06 was fixing, just in machine-readable form: Google can surface `availableLanguage` in rich results, so this was still telling search engines (and anyone who views source) that Hebrew-speaking support is available.
found_and_fixed.fix: Changed to `availableLanguage: ["en", "ru"]`, matching the other 6 places already fixed. Confirmed no other "he"/Hebrew-as-a-spoken-language reference remains anywhere in .ts/.tsx (the one intentionally-kept exception, the Hebrew SEO keyword phrase in app/layout.tsx's metadata keywords array, is unrelated -- it's a discovery keyword for Hebrew-reading searchers, not a support-language claim, as mobile-fixes.json already reasoned through).
found_and_fixed.verified: Confirmed via curl against a live dev server that the rendered <script type="application/ld+json"> now shows `"availableLanguage":["en","ru"]`. Full lint/tsc/build/test suite re-run clean after the change.

flagged_needs_human_input.title: Car-availability lookup fails open (shows all cars available) on any DB error -- same failure mode as the incident earlier this session
flagged_needs_human_input.severity: flagged, not fixed -- business-risk judgment call, deliberately not touched
flagged_needs_human_input.detail: app/lib/availability.ts's getActiveCarBookings() wraps its Prisma query in try/catch; on any error it logs to console.error and returns an empty array (`[]`), i.e. 'no cars are booked.' This is the exact mechanism that made the earlier schema-mismatch incident this session silently show all cars as available regardless of real bookings (per mobile-fixes.json's critical_discovery). That specific incident is fixed (the schema mismatch is resolved and the branch's own migrations were applied), but the underlying fail-open pattern in the catch block is unchanged -- any future error hitting this query (a transient DB blip, a connection-pool exhaustion, a future schema drift, an Upstash/Prisma dependency bump) will again silently make every car look available, which is the worst failure mode for a booking site: it allows real double-bookings to be created with no visible error to staff or customers.
flagged_needs_human_input.why_not_fixed: Changing this to fail closed (e.g. show no cars, or show a maintenance banner, on error) is a genuine product/business trade-off, not a mechanical bug fix: fail-open risks double-bookings during an outage; fail-closed risks losing all bookings during a transient blip. Given this exact code path already caused a serious silent-production-bug incident earlier this session, this felt like exactly the kind of decision the task's guardrails asked to flag rather than act on unilaterally.
options_for_the_owner: Fail closed: on error, treat every car as unavailable (or hide the booking form / show 'temporarily unable to check availability, please call') instead of silently allowing bookings through.

Fail open but alerted: keep current behavior, but wire the console.error into a real alert (email/Telegram, alongside the booking-notification channel already scoped in FOLLOWUP.md's FEAT-01) so a DB error is never silent again.
Leave as-is if the owner considers a rare transient DB error less costly than ever showing 'no cars available' by mistake -- but this should be an explicit decision, not a default.
